messages:
megan: seeing a sudden spike in 5xx from hosted inference gateway in us-east-1 — started ~2m ago. dashboard shows 502/504 wave and tail latency climbing. Can someone confirm?
jamal: on it, pulling logs now. do we have a release id around that time?
sre-oncall: I see increased 502s hitting /v1/generate, errors look like upstream timeouts from runtime: 
```
{"timestamp":"2024-11-04T15:12:30Z","code":502,"upstream":"inference-runtime-27","msg":"request timed out waiting for response"}
```
alex: deploy-bot shows a partial rollout started at 2045012320 — config flag flip `enable-new-routing=true` to 10% traffic.
megan: ugh that flag touched routing rules, right? could be sending some traffic to a new routing tier that wasn't fully warmed.
jamal: confirming — routing rules now route L7->dedicated-group-b where runtime is on a new kernel build. local logs show backlog on that group. queue depth spiking.
sre-oncall: worth rolling that flag back. support-ops already getting customer escalations: 5 customers reported errors in last 5m, one reported timeouts in critical path.
support-ops: forwarding sample customer repro: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"test"}' returns 502 consistently for one tenant.
infra: I can run an immediate rollback of the feature flag if we greenlight. we should also check canary traffic split — maybe the 10% concentrated on a subset of backend hosts.
alex: can we confirm host-level errors? vm logs show kernel panic-like OOMs on two nodes in dedicated-group-b around rollout start. root cause might be an incompatible kernel optimization in the new runtime image.
megan: okay decision: rollback flag to false across regions, pause rollout, and take dedicated-group-b out of rotation. jamal, can you prepare rollback commands?
jamal: running: 
```
# rollback feature flag
redwood-flagctl set enable-new-routing false --env=prod --scope=global
# drain affected pool
redwoodctl pool drain dedicated-group-b --grace-period=30
```
deploy-bot: [deploy bot] Feature flag change recorded: enable-new-routing=false by jamal at 2045012375. Automated canary monitor flagged rollback event.
infra: draining initiated, starting to reprovision fallback kernels on replaced nodes.
sre-oncall: I'm watching error rate — starting to trend down but still elevated. pre-rollback 5xx ~3.8% now 1.4% and falling.
megan: message to customers: pls let support-ops post an update. include mitigation and ETA.
support-ops: posted customer note and created follow-ups for affected accounts. some wanted billing protection — can we enable error-credit for last 30m for tenants who saw >2% error?
megan: yes approve, finance notified.
jamal: after rollback I'm seeing runtimes on dedicated-group-b accepted zero new requests. verifying backpressure cleared. logs now show normal latencies: p50 ~85ms, p95 ~420ms (still a bit high due to in-flight backlog).
infra: we should open a postmortem for the kernel/runtime compatibility matrix and add a pre-rollout smoke test that hits dedicated-group pools with synthetic longer sequences to exercise KV cache.
megan: agreed. action items: (1) infra run full kernel compatibility test (owner infra) (2) add pre-rollout smoke job in deploy pipeline (owner eng-runtime) (3) update canary policy to surface pool-level failures earlier (owner eng-sre) (4) billing credits (owner finance + support).
alex: logging thread. we'll mark incident mitigated once 5xx <0.2% for 30m.
sre-oncall: marking mitigated at 2045012595 (5xx at 0.12%). final note: root cause likely bad interaction between new kernel optimizations and KV cache memory accounting under specific sequence-length distributions.
megan: thanks everyone — great cross-team coordination. I'll start the postmortem doc. :thumbsup:
